requirement.requirement: Every HTTP 426 Upgrade Required response on every server in every environment must include the status code (426) in the response body text. The user/client must see the numeric code in the message, not just the header.

requirement.requirement: The session token display MUST separate the nonce from the GUID so a human can visually verify each part. The display MUST show: (1) Signed token (the encrypted signature), (2) Nonce (the two timestamps extracted from the token), (3) GUID (the session identifier extracted from the token). The nonce and GUID MUST be displayed as separate labeled fields. The presentation in the right panel (after EvaluateCare or SharedServices handoff) MUST be identical to the presentation in the left panel. Both panels MUST use the same labels, layout, and format.
requirement.name: Display nonce and GUID as separate labeled fields with identical format in both

requirement.requirement: For non-production environments (local, dev, qa), if session-token verification or mutual-authentication handshake (per EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-T-002) fails to complete or does not return a definitive VERIFIED/FAILED result within 30 seconds, the state is illegal. The UI MUST render a 'Fatal Error' splash in the center panel and display Verified: FAILED in the session verification panel. The UI MUST NOT display 'Pending' for longer than 30 seconds. In production, any runtime security-primitive failure MUST cause the hard process exit defined in EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-T-004.
requirement.name: Render Fatal Error splash if session authentication fails or times out in non‑PR

requirement.requirement: The session-verification panel rendered in the left (specialty search / guiSessionCell) and right panels MUST include two additional rows below the existing fields: (1) `Env: <ENV>` where ENV is the environment label (LOCAL, DEV, QA, or PROD) of the service that issued the token, derived from the active deployment context; (2) `Time: PST <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS>` where the value is the token's `created_at` timestamp reformatted to America/Los_Angeles timezone (Pacific Time, observing daylight saving). Both rows MUST appear in both the left and right panel renderings so a human operator can verify which environment served the token and at what time without consulting external tools.
requirement.name: Session token display must include Env and PST Time rows in both panels

requirement.requirement: The session_token.origin field returned by /verify-token (and any equivalent endpoint that returns a session_token object) MUST be set to the name of the RESPONDING service (e.g., "EvaluateCare" for EvaluateCare's /verify-token; "SharedServices" for SharedServices'). This origin field is the SELF-IDENTIFICATION of the service that produced THIS response object — it is distinct from the cryptographic token signer (REQ-017, which always identifies FindCare). One service MUST NOT assert another service's identity in any field rendered to the operator. The wrapper's session-verification panel MUST render this origin value as-is, treating it as the responding service's authoritative claim of its own identity. The display proves that the named component received the nonce and token and produced this verification result.
requirement.name: verify-token response origin field self-identifies the responding service

requirement.requirement: Session token mutual authentication MUST pass for SharedServices. The same token FindCare created MUST be the same one SharedServices received.
requirement.name: Enforce SharedServices mutual auth using FindCare-created session token

requirement.requirement: Any call from FindCare, EvaluateCare, or SharedServices to one another MUST complete a mutual-authentication TLS 1.2+ handshake. A failed or incomplete handshake is a fatal error per EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-B-008.
requirement.name: Mutual-authentication TLS 1.2+ for FindCare, EvaluateCare, SharedServices inter-

requirement.requirement: The session token MUST use a stable GUID that identifies the session for its lifetime. The nonce (timestamps) MUST be regenerated fresh on every inter-service call. The GUID MUST NOT change between calls within the same session. The nonce MUST NOT be reused across calls. Every ChatHealthy component (FindCare, EvaluateCare, SharedServices) that receives a token MUST update the last_used timestamp in the nonce to prove it processed the token at that time. Reusing a nonce is a replay attack vector and fails NIST 800-53 SC-23 (Session Authenticity).
requirement.name: Session token uses stable GUID and freshly regenerated nonce on each call

requirement.requirement: On startup every server MUST exercise each security primitive it uses (session-token generation, signature signing and verification, credential redaction, mTLS handshake, key decryption, authentication check). If any exercise fails the process MUST exit with a non-zero code. A server MUST NOT serve any request after a failed startup exercise. Exit codes: 78 (configuration failure — missing library, missing cert, missing env var, malformed primitive output), 77 (permission denied on cert or key file), 70 (unexpected internal error). Stderr MUST name the primitive that failed.
requirement.name: Startup must test security primitives; exit on failure with specific codes

requirement.requirement: EvaluateCare and SharedServices HF Space deploys MUST include findcare.crt (base64-PEM) as an HF Space Secret named FINDCARE_CERT_PEM. On startup, each backend MUST decode this secret and write it to CERTS_DIR so session_token.verify_session_token can validate incoming tokens signed by FindCare. Absence of this secret is a fatal error per EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-B-008.
requirement.name: Deploy findcare.crt as FINDCARE_CERT_PEM secret and decode to CERTS_DIR on start

requirement.requirement: Every session token generated by a ChatHealthy service MUST include an `origin` field whose value is the name of the originating service (FindCare, EvaluateCare, or SharedServices). The token's signature MUST be produced with that service's own private key. Any service receiving a token MUST verify the signature using the named origin's public certificate and MUST reject the token if the origin field does not match the signing key. The session token display — both the left panel at creation and the right panel after a cross-service handoff — MUST render the origin value as a labeled field so a human can visually confirm which service signed the token.
requirement.name: Session token must include and display service origin, signed and verified per-s

requirement.requirement: When the user transfers page ownership to EvaluateCare or SharedServices, the right-panel mutual-authentication request (/verify-token) MUST be issued by the browser directly to the cold-button service (the new owner) and MUST NOT be proxied through FindCare. The browser MUST use the cold service's environment-specific URL (HF Space URL for dev/qa/prod, https://localhost:PORT for local) as the request target. The cold service's /verify-token response — including the verified session token — MUST be the source of the data rendered in the right panel. This ensures the right panel reflects the actual active service's verification, not FindCare's proxied view of it, and is independently verifiable by inspecting the browser DevTools Network tab. CORS on EvaluateCare and SharedServices MUST allow the wrapper origins (localhost, dev.chathealthy.ai, qa.chathealthy.ai, chathealthy.ai). The /session call (token issuance) MUST continue to target FindCare since FindCare is the sole token issuer. Verification: Code/deploy/localSmokeTestPyTest.py and Code/deploy/devSmokeTestPyTest.py TestStep25.test_push_shared_services MUST register a network listener before the SharedServices banner button click and assert (a) at least one POST to SHARED_URL+'/verify-token' (direct call) and (b) zero POSTs ending in '/shared/verify-token' (no proxy). See BUG-VERIFY-TOKEN-PROXY-001.
requirement.name: Browser must call cold-button service directly for verify-token (no FindCare proxy)

epic.name: ChatHealthy FrontEnd libary
epic.description: Shared Python library distributed as the pip package `chathealthy-frontend-lib` (repo root: `FrontEndApplicationLib/`). Owns the code consumed in common by ChatHealthy.ai's front-end-facing services (FindCare, EvaluateCare, SharedServices) and the wrapper. Scope is FRONT-END application code only — devops, data pipelines, and analytics are explicitly out of scope. Operating-model intent: a separate team with its own P&L manages this library; consumers depend on it via versioned releases (`pip install chathealthy-frontend-lib==X.Y.Z`) following standard industry convention for shared libraries, including the boundary that the package mints no auth tokens — auth-token MANUFACTURE belongs 100% to SharedServices; only auth-token MANAGEMENT (verification, parsing, nonce advancement) is shared and lives here.

feature.name: Shared front-end UX widget library
feature.description: Distribution mechanism + source-of-truth for the display-only UX widgets currently inlined in Website/index.html and the FindCare React iframe. Includes the chFatalError full-screen overlay, the non-prod env banner, the non-prod security panel (right-side rightSecurity panel), and any future widget shared by more than one front-end consumer. The library carries NO business logic — peer selection, mutual-auth pairing, service routing, ownership state, and any other biz-logic concerns are explicitly excluded and live in the backend per the no-biz-logic-on-client rule. Distribution channel TBD (npm package, CDN-hosted versioned bundle, or repo-internal copy at deploy time) — to be decided as part of the first story under this feature. Owned by the same EPIC-003 team that owns chathealthy-frontend-lib (Python).

feature.name: Backend orchestration that supports the shared front-end UX widgets
feature.description: Backend endpoints + service-layer code that own all the business logic that today lives inline in Website/index.html and the FindCare React iframe — peer selection (which backend's /health to call), mutual-auth pairing (the /session-then-/verify-token sequence currently driven from the wrapper), service-routing/ownership-state (gotoFindCare/gotoEvaluateCare/gotoSharedServices and the underlying ownership transition), and any other biz-logic decision the wrapper is making today. The widgets in EPIC-003-F-001 then become pure display: each widget consumes ONE clean data endpoint per render. This feature exists so that the no-biz-logic-on-client rule can actually be enforced; without it, extracting widgets only relocates the violation, not removes it. Per the auth caveat, token MANUFACTURE belongs 100% to SharedServices and any orchestration here MUST respect that boundary.

story.description: The prime engineering rule lives only in CLAUDE.md today and has no hook-driven enforcement. This story moves the rule text verbatim into engineering_rules.json and adds two runtime enforcement entries that execute via the existing hook architecture: prompt_verify_directive (UserPromptSubmit) and response_claim_audit (Stop). requirement.requirement: Above all else: Claude MUST NOT make any misrepresentations. Before stating anything, Claude must conduct sufficient research - reading project files, code, requirements, and external sources as needed - so that Claude can only: state a verified fact, state that it does not know, or ask a clarifying question. Materiality threshold
requirement.requirement: In all non-production environments, a possible consequence to an action a human user asks Claude Code to do - either as an analysis task or as one that will change state in a reversible way - must not be surfaced to the human operator when that possible analytical or factual potential has less than a 2% probability of occurring.

The prime rule MUST be encoded as a Rule entry in brain/machine_artifacts/content/engineering_rules.json with at least two enforcement entries that execute at runtime via the existing hook architecture: (1) prompt_verify_directive fires on UserPromptSubmit and, when the user prompt asks about external-system behavior, injects a hard directive requiring Claude to cite a tool result from this turn or to say 'I don't know - let me verify'; (2) response_claim_audit fires on Stop, scans Claude's just-finished response for definitive claims about external systems, and writes a violation record when no Read/Grep/Bash/WebFetch tool call in the same turn touched that system. Both executors live inside the renamed hook manager (AnthropicsClaudeCodeHookManager.py). The CLAUDE.md preamble is replaced by a one-line pointer to the rule ID.
requirement.name: Prime rule runtime enforcement

story.name: Rules infrastructure: manager, base worker, lock, timeout, telemetry, exit-code aggregation
story.description: ChatHealthyEnforcementManager + EnforcementWorker (abstract base) deliver the framework: read-only rules-registry load, hook-filtered enforcement dispatch, manager-owned mutex coordination, per-worker subprocess timeout, structured violation/telemetry envelopes, and worst-code-wins aggregation. Per V20 §4.4. The manager is invoked by every Git and Claude Code hook with a single hook_name argument.

requirement.name: Rules carry enforcement entries
requirement.requirement: Every engineering rule that the team intends to enforce MUST carry at least one programmatic enforcement entry. A rule with an empty enforcement array is documentation, not governance, and SHALL be either populated, retired, or annotated as documentation-only.

requirement.name: Enforcement at hook moment
requirement.requirement: Enforcement runs at the moment a violation can occur — the relevant Git or Claude Code hook — not on a separate cadence. There is no nightly job that catches yesterday's mistake.

requirement.name: Hook-agnostic framework
requirement.requirement: An engineering rule MUST be able to attach to any of the four Git hooks (pre-commit, commit-msg, post-commit, pre-push) and any of the six Claude Code hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd, InstructionsLoaded). The framework is hook-agnostic; the enforcement entry declares its hook.

requirement.name: Human debuggability
requirement.requirement: The system MUST be debuggable by a human. One file per role. One class per file. One entry point. Per-enforcement, per-worker structured stdout and telemetry, with worst exit code propagated.

requirement.name: Multi-PID concurrency
requirement.requirement: The framework MUST handle multi-PID race conditions correctly. The same hook can fire many times concurrently across different Claude Code PIDs and Git invocations. The manager acquires a lock before dispatching any worker whose enforcement entry declares requires_lock = True; in-process locks are forbidden.

requirement.name: Additive enforcement
requirement.requirement: Adding the next enforcement MUST be a small, additive change. New enforcement entries get a new enforcement_id and — if needed — a new worker subclass; existing rules and workers are not touched.

requirement.name: Worker inherits base class
requirement.requirement: Every worker MUST inherit from EnforcementWorker. Subclasses implement only their domain-specific check logic. The base class owns scope evaluation, violation shape, exit codes, telemetry, and error handling so every worker behaves the same from the manager's perspective.

requirement.name: Enforcement entry first-class
requirement.requirement: Enforcement entries are first-class records: every entry carries a stable enforcement_id (format <rule_id>-ENF-NNN), a declared hook, an executable_path, a scopes field carrying scope-list rules in the four canonical types (allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern), and a requires_lock boolean. They can be cited in audit trails, bug reports, and the backlog like requirements are today.

requirement.name: Filesystem mirrors operating model
requirement.requirement: The architecture MUST be aligned with the EPIC / Feature / Story tree. Filesystem mirrors operating model. The home for this feature is projectRoot/architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/. crossEpicConcerns/ holds shared business artifacts only — no code lives there.

requirement.name: V1 demonstrability
requirement.requirement: Once V1 ships, BR-1 through BR-9 are demonstrably satisfied for the worked example (file scanning on pre-commit) and the framework is in place to absorb every other rule on its own schedule.

requirement.name: Four canonical scope-list types
requirement.requirement: The framework MUST support all four scope-list types on every enforcement entry, even when a given worker uses only a subset. The four permitted terms (allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern) are the only vocabulary used anywhere in this system.

requirement.name: Enforcement schema fields
requirement.requirement: engineering_rules.json schema gains the following required fields per enforcement entry: enforcement_id (string, format <rule_id>-ENF-NNN); hook (enum: pre-commit, commit-msg, post-commit, pre-push, SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd, InstructionsLoaded); executable_path (string — repo-relative path to the worker script that implements this enforcement); requires_lock (boolean — true if the manager must acquire a lock before dispatching this worker); scopes (array of three-column arrays — [function_name: str, scope_list_type: str, list_of_terms: list[str]] — carrying this enforcement's per-enforcement scope-list rules; scope_list_type ∈ {allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern}; the EngineeringRulesSchema.json validator enforces this row shape; see §4.6); timeout (integer, optional — seconds; defaults to manager constant DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30 when omitted; the manager passes this value to subprocess.run(..., timeout=N); on timeout the manager kills the worker subprocess and returns EXIT_WORKER_TIMEOUT (4); the worker does not see this field — the timeout is enforced by the parent process; see §4.3.2). The four scope-list types are carried only by scopes; there are no separate top-level allowed_exact / allowed_pattern / excluded_exact / excluded_pattern fields on the entry.

requirement.name: Manager class and exit codes
requirement.requirement: ChatHealthyEnforcementManager lives at projectRoot/architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py. Single class. Single main(). Constructor signature __init__(hook_name: str). run() returns int. The manager module defines the following named exit-code constants and run() returns one of them: EXIT_OK = 0 (all matched enforcements passed), EXIT_VIOLATIONS_FOUND = 1 (at least one worker reported violations; commit/push must block), EXIT_MANAGER_ERROR = 2 (manager-level failure: cannot read engineering_rules.json, malformed schema, unknown hook name, or any other pre-dispatch error), EXIT_WORKER_SPAWN_FAILURE = 3 (one or more workers could not be launched: missing executable_path, executable not found, permission denied, OSError on subprocess), EXIT_WORKER_TIMEOUT = 4 (one or more workers exceeded the configured subprocess timeout), EXIT_WORKER_INTERNAL_ERROR = 5 (a worker exited with a non-0 / non-1 status — i.e. anything ≥ 3 from a worker is treated as an internal worker failure rather than a violation). Aggregation by precedence (highest wins): 2 > 3 > 5 > 4 > 1 > 0. Manager-level errors trump worker errors trump violations trump success, so the caller can immediately tell whether the issue is in the framework or in the user's code. Worker exit codes follow the same convention for the worker's subset: 0 = clean, 1 = violations, 2 = worker error; any worker exit ≥ 3 is promoted by the manager to EXIT_WORKER_INTERNAL_ERROR.

requirement.name: Manager load-filter-spawn
requirement.requirement: Manager loads engineering_rules.json read-only, filters enforcement[] by hook, and for each matching enforcement reads executable_path and spawns the worker via subprocess.run([sys.executable, executable_path, enforcement_id], timeout=...). The manager collects each subprocess returncode and aggregates by the TR-2 exit-code precedence.

requirement.name: EnforcementWorker base class
requirement.requirement: EnforcementWorker (abstract base) lives at architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/enforcement_worker.py. It owns: __init__(enforcement_id), _load_enforcement(), is_in_scope(resource), main() (CLI entry that parses enforcement_id, instantiates the subclass, calls run(), returns its exit code), violation emission, telemetry emission, and structured error handling. Subclasses implement run() and any private helper methods their domain requires.

requirement.name: Violation record shape
requirement.requirement: Violation record shape (emitted by the base class): {enforcement_id, rule_id, resource, message, severity}. severity in {info, warn, error}.

requirement.name: Telemetry envelope
requirement.requirement: Telemetry envelope (emitted by the base class): start record and end record per worker invocation, both carrying enforcement_id, hook, duration_ms, files_scanned, violation_count, exit_code. Format: one JSON object per line to stdout.

requirement.name: Manager-owned mutex
requirement.requirement: When an enforcement entry declares requires_lock = True, the manager MUST acquire a process-safe lock keyed on enforcement_id before invoking subprocess.run, and MUST release the lock after subprocess.run returns (clean, non-zero, or timeout). Default mechanism: advisory file lock. In-process Python locks are forbidden. Workers do not declare a concurrency primitive.

requirement.name: Manager-worker contract
requirement.requirement: Manager and workers MUST NOT import each other's internals. The only contract is enforcement_id (str) in via CLI argv, exit code (int) out via subprocess returncode, and the structured stdout (violation + telemetry) envelope.

requirement.name: Tests location
requirement.requirement: Tests live at architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/tests/. The base class ships with its own test suite covering scope evaluation, exit-code semantics, violation shape, telemetry envelope, and the try/except fail-safe. Each new worker ships with at least one happy-path and one violation-path test.

requirement.name: Hook plumbing
requirement.requirement: Hook plumbing. .git/hooks/{pre-commit, commit-msg, post-commit, pre-push} each invoke `python <repo-root>/architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py --hook <hook>`. .claude/settings.json registers the same invocation under SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd, InstructionsLoaded with the matching `--hook <hook_name>` flag. A pytest under architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/tests/ MUST verify, for every hook named above: (a) hard assert the wire-up exists when the hook carries at least one enforcement entry in engineering_rules.json; (b) advisory warning when the wire-up is missing and the hook has no enforcement (reserved for future Phase-6 workers). The test runs in the F-002 suite and the hard assertions gate pre-push.

requirement.name: Worker taxonomy
requirement.requirement: Worker taxonomy supported by the framework: file scanning (pre-commit / pre-push), prompt-injection check (UserPromptSubmit — returns additionalContext), post-response audit (Stop), log publishing (UserPromptSubmit + Stop -> Kafka), boot orchestration (SessionStart), and mode selection (SessionStart). Each is a concrete subclass of EnforcementWorker, deployed as its own standalone executable.

story.name: Scanning: file enumeration on hooks, SCOPES evaluation, scope precedence
story.description: Per V20 §4.5 and §4.9. Workers receive resource candidates (staged or about-to-push files for the V1 ScanFilesEnforcementWorker), evaluate each via the base-class is_in_scope() walk against the SCOPES rows on the enforcement entry, and dispatch matched check methods. Scope precedence is fixed and lives entirely in the base class.

requirement.name: Scope walk precedence
requirement.requirement: Scope evaluation is fixed-precedence and lives entirely in the base class. For each (resource, function_name) the base class walks the matching rows in self.scopes (filtered by function_name) in this fixed order: excluded_exact, excluded_pattern, allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, then per-check SCOPE_DEFAULT. Subclasses do not override this walk. The default behavior (in scope vs. out of scope when no row matched) is declared per check via the per-method SCOPE_DEFAULT class attribute.

requirement.name: ScanFilesEnforcementWorker
requirement.requirement: ScanFilesEnforcementWorker (worked example, V1) lives at projectRoot/architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/scan_files_enforcement_worker.py. It is a standalone Python script with a main() that takes enforcement_id as a CLI argument and exits with a status code. Its run() implements two domain checks synchronously, in this order, on every in-scope file: (a) _scan_http(file) — the HTTP-vs-HTTPS regex scan ported from preCommitScan.py; (b) _validate_json(file) — the JSON schema validation ported from validate_all_json.py. Both run inside the same subprocess. Multi-threading inside run() is a documented future enhancement, not V1. requires_lock = false (read-only worker; the manager dispatches without acquiring a lock). ScanFilesEnforcementWorker's scope-list rules live in its enforcement entry in engineering_rules.json under the scopes field (see §4.6); the worker inherits the default _load_scopes() from EnforcementWorker, which returns self.entry.get("scopes", []). It does NOT override _load_scopes() and contributes no SCOPES class attribute (see §4.5 for the mechanism, §4.9.1 for the per-method spec, and §4.9.2 for the worked-example rows).

requirement.name: Scope rows on enforcement entry
requirement.requirement: ScanFilesEnforcementWorker scope rules are expressed as a flat three-column list in its enforcement entry in engineering_rules.json under the scopes field. Each row has the shape [function_name: str, scope_list_type: str, list_of_terms: list[str]] where scope_list_type is one of the four canonical terms (allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern) and function_name is the name of a check method on the worker (e.g. _scan_http, _validate_json). The EnforcementWorker base class loads the list at worker startup through the virtual _load_scopes() method, whose default implementation returns self.entry.get("scopes", []); ScanFilesEnforcementWorker inherits that default and does NOT override it. The base class then resolves function_name to a bound method via getattr(self, row[0]) at startup, so a typo in function_name fails loudly rather than silently dropping a rule. The ordered precedence of the four types is fixed in the base class per TR-5 and is described in narrative form in §4.5. The SCOPE_DEFAULT class attribute is per-check: False for _scan_http (don't flag a path that no rule matched), True for _validate_json (every governed JSON is in scope unless explicitly excluded). The canonical worked example — exactly the rows used by V1 — is in §4.9.2.

requirement.name: preCommitScan.py JSON retirement
requirement.requirement: preCommitScan.py SHALL drop ".json" from SCAN_EXTENSIONS and \.json$ from HTTP_EXEMPT_PATTERNS once ScanFilesEnforcementWorker is the single source of truth (note: SCAN_EXTENSIONS and HTTP_EXEMPT_PATTERNS are legacy module-level names inside preCommitScan.py — the artifact being retired — and are not part of the new framework's vocabulary; the new framework uses scopes rows in engineering_rules.json). Once the manager dispatches all enforcement, preCommitScan.py is retired.

story.name: HTTP vs HTTPS: _scan_http check and allowed_pattern URL handling
story.description: Per V20 BR-12, BR-13, TR-11. The _scan_http check on ScanFilesEnforcementWorker enforces that production source code, documentation, and deployment configuration MUST NOT contain http:// URLs unless the URL itself matches an allowed_pattern row on the enforcement entry's scopes (loopback, link-local metadata, w3.org, etc.). Files intended to carry http:// content as legitimate data are listed in allowed_exact / allowed_pattern rows. Other files are exempted via excluded_exact / excluded_pattern.

requirement.name: http: legitimate-content allowance
requirement.requirement: Files that are intended to carry plain text "http:" as legitimate content — for example, JSON files whose purpose is to record example URLs, configuration files that list http endpoints by design, fixtures, and similar data files — MUST be allowed to contain the term "http:". These files are listed on the enforcement entry's allowed by exact match rows, or matched by the enforcement entry's allowed by pattern rows, and they will not be flagged as a violation.

requirement.name: http: production-source ban
requirement.requirement: Files that are intended to be production source code, documentation, deployment configuration, or any other artifact that should not embed insecure http URLs MUST NOT contain the term "http:" unless the URL itself is on the enforcement entry's allowed by pattern rows (for example, loopback addresses, link-local metadata endpoints, or known public standards URLs). Files of this kind that are deliberately exempt for any reason MUST appear on the enforcement entry's excluded by exact match rows or be matched by the enforcement entry's excluded by pattern rows. Any other file found to contain the term "http:" is a violation and the commit MUST be blocked.

requirement.name: _scan_http scope alignment
requirement.requirement: The set of files allowed to contain "http:" is exactly the union of the enforcement entry's allowed_exact rows and the files matched by the entry's allowed_pattern rows for _scan_http. The set of files exempt from the scan entirely is exactly the union of the entry's excluded_exact rows and the files matched by the entry's excluded_pattern rows for _scan_http. Any file not matched by any of those four scope_list_type rows that contains the term "http:" — except where the URL itself matches an allowed_pattern row for _scan_http — is a violation.

story.name: JSON validation: _validate_json check, $schema web-fetch resolver, meta-schema carve-out, in-run cache
story.description: Per V20 BR-11/15/16, TR-12/18/19, §4.9.3 and §4.9.3.1. The _validate_json check on ScanFilesEnforcementWorker validates every governed JSON file under brain/machine_artifacts/content/ against the schema declared in its $schema field, using jsonschema Draft 2020-12. ChatHealthy schemas declared in $schema URLs are resolved via HTTPS GET (5s timeout, per-run cache) per TR-18; the JSON Schema 2020-12 meta-schema is the single carve-out, served from a local copy under Website/schemas/standard/ per TR-19 / BR-16. Files with $schema missing that are not explicitly excluded MUST FAIL LOUD.

requirement.name: Governed JSON validation gate
requirement.requirement: Every file the system treats as governed JSON content MUST validate cleanly against the schema declared in its $schema field. The set of governed JSON files is defined using only the four permitted scope-list terms (allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern). The system MUST NOT trust data from a JSON file that fails schema validation, and the framework MUST treat validation failure as a governance violation. JSON validation is the load-bearing gate that protects the entire governed-data layer from silent drift.

requirement.name: Draft 2020-12, no opt-out
requirement.requirement: Governed JSON content lives under brain/machine_artifacts/content/. Each governed JSON file MUST declare its schema URL in a top-level $schema field. JSON parsing uses Python's standard library json module. Schema validation uses the jsonschema package against JSON Schema Draft 2020-12. Validation failure produces a violation record per TR-6 and contributes to the worker's exit code (EXIT_VIOLATIONS_FOUND = 1). Files identified by the worker's excluded_exact or excluded_pattern lists are skipped silently; files in scope without a $schema field MUST FAIL LOUD. There is no opt-out, and there is no quiet passing of unschemaed JSON content. The JSON Schema 2020-12 meta-schema URL is the single resolver carve-out, served from a local copy at Website/schemas/standard/json-schema-2020-12-meta.json. All other $schema URLs are resolved by HTTP GET with a 5-second timeout and per-run cache.

requirement.name: Validation uses $schema URL
requirement.requirement: Validation MUST use the schema referenced by the JSON file's $schema URL.

requirement.name: External standards committed
requirement.requirement: External standards used by the framework MUST be committed to the repository.

requirement.name: $schema HTTPS resolution + cache
requirement.requirement: Aligned to BR-15. ChatHealthy schemas declared in $schema URLs are resolved via HTTPS GET to the URL the JSON file declared, performed at validation time. A per-run cache deduplicates identical URLs within a single worker invocation. Unreachable URL, non-200, timeout, or non-JSON response body produces a per-file ViolationRecord per TR-6.

requirement.name: External-standard carve-out cache
requirement.requirement: Aligned to BR-16. Cached external standards live under Website/schemas/standard/. A standard is eligible for caching when its URL is contractually frozen by the spec maintainer (any change requires a new versioned URL). The framework's runtime serves those URLs from the cached copies. Cached standards remain under the stewardship of their original publisher; the framework's governance applies to content the framework owns.

feature.name: Brain Consistency
feature.description: Ensures all brain JSON data is internally consistent, cross-referenced, and free of orphaned records. Enforcement mechanisms run deterministically on boot and at check-in.

story.description: On the first user prompt, Claude Code MUST boot the governance singleton and ask the user to select an operating mode (1 = Unattended, 2 = Normal, 3 = Idiot). There MUST be no SessionStart hook. Known bug: BUG-AUTH-001.

requirement.requirement: CLAUDE.md MUST state only that the boot class governs the session.
requirement.name: CLAUDE.md states only that boot class governs the session

requirement.requirement: Each Claude Code session MUST complete a deterministic, non-circumventable boot sequence before any other work. The sequence is: (1) load the governance brain and run compliance checks; (2) at the end of boot, ask the user exactly two questions in order and block all other assistant output until both are answered — Q1: mode selection per REQ-010; Q2: orphan triage per REQ-011. The sequence MUST NOT be skippable, paraphrasable, summarizable, or deferrable by Claude Code. Implementation MAY use any hook topology (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop-hook validator, blocking-reply pattern) so long as the user-observable behavior holds: every new session begins with those two questions presented verbatim, in order, with no other assistant output preceding them.
requirement.name: Enforce deterministic boot: governance + 2 mandatory verbatim questions before I

requirement.requirement: After boot completes, Claude Code MUST ask the user to select an operating mode: 1 = Unattended, 2 = Normal, 3 = Idiot. Claude Code MUST NOT proceed until the user has made a selection.
requirement.name: Prompt user to select mode after boot; block execution until selection is made

requirement.requirement: Orphan triage is the second of the two boot questions. After the user answers REQ-010, Claude Code MUST ask a single yes/no question: 'Triage orphan bugs?' If the user answers no, boot completes and normal work begins. If the user answers yes, Claude Code MUST present the orphan bug table and the user chooses how many to triage this boot — one, several, or all. Triaging an orphan means assigning it a req_id or closing it. There is no per-orphan defer option and no obligation to triage every orphan; the single yes/no gate governs whether the list is shown at all, and within 'yes' the user drives how many get worked.
requirement.name: Boot question: Ask user 'Triage orphan bugs?' and present table if answered yes

requirement.requirement: Every action taken within this project MUST be governed by any applicable rule found in brain/machine_artifacts/content/engineering_rules.json. These engineering rules MUST be in Claude's 1,000,000 token context and MUST be checked before any action for compliance. If an order from a human or a task Claude or an agent of Claude contradicts any rules, Claude CANNOT take that action or follow that order.
requirement.name: Enforce compliance with engineering_rules.json before any action is taken

requirement.requirement: The user MUST NOT be forced to login twice during the boot sequence. A single interactive login event per identity provider is the limit; a second consecutive prompt for the same user to the same provider within one boot is a failure. If the first login produced a valid session or cached credential, the boot sequence MUST reuse that credential rather than re-prompt.
requirement.name: Prevent duplicate login prompts per identity provider during one boot sequence

requirement.requirement: The boot class MUST be a single Python file with __main__ and a chathealthy_devops_boot class. main() dispatches to the class by mode (prompt, tool_call, prompt_result, session_end). There is no boot mode — boot is triggered by the prompt handler on first call. Every mode handler MUST be wrapped in try/except/finally. The finally block MUST always call sys.exit() to return control to Cursor/Claude Code. All modes MUST fail open on exception.
requirement.name: Single Python boot class file with strict handler and exit constraints

requirement.requirement: inform_claude() MUST serialize singleton state (version, framework, build, brain file list, constraints, non-allow governance matrix cells) and the orphan table into additionalContext in the hook response. Called from the prompt() path on first boot.
requirement.name: Serialize singleton state and orphan table into additionalContext on first boot

requirement.requirement: chathealthyai_brainboot.json MUST be deleted. brain/machine_artifacts/boot/ directory MUST be deleted. All references to both in chathealthy_devops_boot.py and governance_matrix.json MUST be removed.
requirement.name: Delete chathealthyai_brainboot.json and boot dir, remove all references in code

requirement.requirement: Boot MUST only occur once per session. On SessionEnd, the boot flag in .claude/ChatHealthySettings.json MUST be set to FALSE. On a successful boot from within Anthropic's UserPromptSubmit hook, the flag MUST be set to TRUE. Each subsequent call from the hook MUST check the flag to determine whether the session needs to be booted. If ChatHealthySettings.json or the boot flag cannot be found, an error message MUST be output to the user and no boot is attempted. If SessionEnd does not fire (crash, force-quit), the next session's first prompt will hit the error state and inform the user.
requirement.name: Enforce single boot per session using boot flag in ChatHealthySettings.json

requirement.requirement: SessionEnd hook MUST clear the booted flag in .claude/ChatHealthySettings.json on every invocation. SessionEnd MUST be wrapped in try/except/finally and MUST fail open. SessionEnd is known not to fire on Cursor window-close or auto-compaction; the SessionStart hook (REQ-007) is the primary clearer, and SessionEnd is the secondary clearer for clean exits (/logout, /exit, /clear).
requirement.name: SessionEnd hook clears booted flag in ChatHealthySettings.json, fails open

requirement.requirement: Three context-resident artifacts MUST be loaded into the Claude Code session context at every session start, and MUST be re-injected after any context compaction: (1) brain/machine_artifacts/content/bugs.json — active bug register, loaded in full; (2) brain/machine_artifacts/content/engineering_rules.json — engineering rules, loaded in full; (3) test_output/backlog_stories.json — story-level pruned view of agile_backlog.json covering Epic → Feature → Story only. The story view carries story metadata (story_id, title, description, parent_feature, sprint, size, status, accepted_by, orphan, approval) plus an integer requirement_count per story. It does NOT carry requirement bodies, pytest pointers, realized_by arrays, or any node below story. The full agile_backlog.json (~521K tokens) is NOT context-resident; specific requirement bodies, pytest ids, and realized_by data MUST be fetched from the canonical brain/machine_artifacts/content/agile_backlog.json via Read when Claude needs them. Canonical brain content lives on disk under brain/machine_artifacts/content/ and is never stored anywhere else. The story view is a derived artifact — gitignored, regenerated at session start from the canonical source — it does not replace the source. A pytest MUST verify: (a) @-imports for the three context-resident artifacts are present in the root CLAUDE.md; (b) every current file under Code/DataPipelines/ matching the listed extensions (minus excluded dirs) has a corresponding @-import; (c) every @-imported file exists and is non-empty; (d) no @-imported path is stale. A git pre-commit hook MUST regenerate the DataPipelines @-import block when any file under Code/DataPipelines/ is added, moved, or deleted; if the block is stale, pre-commit MUST fail. Purpose: these artifacts are the ones Claude is most prone to shortcut-reasoning about — grepping instead of reading, guessing instead of checking, proposing duplicates because the original was never loaded. Making the backlog's high-level shape (9 epics / 83 features / 301 stories) context-resident removes the option to grep-and-punt for structure. Requirement bodies remain on-demand because loading the full backlog at ~521K tokens would consume more than half the 1M context window for content that is rarely needed in full. History: agile_backlog.json was attempted in context-residency 2026-04-18 and was replaced with the story-level view the same day. EPIC-008-F-003-S-002-REQ-T-003 (the flat pipe-delimited req_index.txt view) is deprecated in favor of this story-tree view. API source: Claude Code memory docs at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md — '@path/to/import' syntax, 'Imported files are expanded and loaded into context at launch', 'CLAUDE.md files are loaded in full regardless of length', 'Project-root CLAUDE.md survives compaction: after /compact, Claude re-reads it from disk and re-injects it into the session.' Hook-based injection is NOT a viable substitute because per https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit hooks cap additionalContext at 10,000 characters with overflow saved to file + preview — too small for these artifacts.
requirement.name: Require key artifacts loaded into Claude Code session context at every start and

requirement.requirement: Per-artifact load confirmation. After each session boot, the diagnostic MUST emit one confirmation line per context-resident artifact as defined in REQ-012. Each line MUST cite the full project-relative path of the artifact. Silent success is not permitted. The diagnostic signal may come from the InstructionsLoaded hook log, a direct content canary, or both; the reporting format is one line per artifact regardless of source. This requirement MUST NOT name specific artifacts — REQ-012 is the single source of truth for the artifact list; any change to scope belongs there, not here.
requirement.name: Emit one confirmation line per context-resident artifact after session boot

requirement.requirement: Load-failure short message. If any context-resident brain artifact fails load verification at session boot (per REQ-012 and REQ-017), the diagnostic MUST output a single short failure line (one line, under 200 characters) that names the failing artifact and classifies the failure as exactly one of four reasons — no more, no less: invalid_json | hash_unreadable | not_loaded | hash_mismatch. A long explanation is a violation of this requirement — follow-up detail belongs in a separate report, not the verdict line.
requirement.name: Short one-line artifact load failure message with exact reason classification

requirement.requirement: Load verification procedure. For each context-resident artifact as defined in REQ-012, the diagnostic MUST execute exactly four steps in order, short-circuiting on the first failure: (1) validate the file as JSON — on failure emit 'invalid_json'; (2) compute sha256 of the file on disk and retain it — on I/O or hash failure emit 'hash_unreadable'; (3) confirm the harness loaded the file into context (InstructionsLoaded event fired for that file_path) — on absence emit 'not_loaded'; (4) recompute sha256 at the InstructionsLoaded event and compare to the hash from step 2 — on inequality emit 'hash_mismatch'. If all four steps pass, emit one 'LOADED' line per REQ-015. These four failure reasons are exhaustive: the diagnostic MUST NOT introduce a fifth category (e.g. timeout, truncation, attention_drift, unknown). Any observed failure that does not map to one of the four reasons is a gap in the procedure, not a new reason. This requirement MUST NOT name specific artifacts — REQ-012 is the single source of truth for the artifact list.
requirement.name: Verify context-resident artifacts using four-step diagnostic with strict error,

requirement.requirement: The Claude Code boot sequence MUST execute 100% from artifacts resident in this project's git repository. No dependency on files outside the repository (user home directory, global Claude Code configuration, machine-level config, external URLs fetched at boot time) is permitted for the boot path. A clean clone of the repository, opened in Claude Code on any machine, MUST boot deterministically to the same governance state as any other. External services (LLM APIs, Cloudflare-hosted schemas, cloud billing dashboards) MAY be contacted after the boot sequence completes, but the boot sequence itself MUST NOT require them.
