story.description: Runtime requirements for the brain — specifically WHERE ChatHealthy.AI brain content is persisted on disk and WHERE it must be at runtime (i.e. loaded into Claude's active context). Brain content lives under brain/machine_artifacts/content/. Files outside that tree, including Claude Code's and Cursor's harness-managed Markdown files (CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/*.md, MEMORY.md and Claude's auto-memory topic files under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/), are NOT brain storage regardless of their content type. At runtime, brain content MUST be accessible to Claude without a disk Read (context-resident, per EPIC-008-F-003-S-001-REQ-T-006). The mechanism is harness-level @-imports from a project-root file (CLAUDE.md) that point at the brain JSONs and derived JSON views of brain JSONs.

requirement.requirement: Before creating any bug record in brain/machine_artifacts/content/bugs.json, Claude MUST search the register for a semantically duplicate or closely-related existing bug and update the existing record rather than create a new one when a match is found. Updates MUST focus on conciseness, accuracy, and fidelity to the evidence. When the bug is novel, Claude MUST insert it under a logical parent requirement (its req_id) in the register. When no logical parent requirement exists: in Normal or Idiot Mode (v4-004) Claude MUST escalate to human and wait for a decision before inserting; in Unattended Mode Claude MUST insert the bug with req_id = ORPHAN_BUG, flag it for human's async review at the next boot's orphan triage, and proceed with its work.
requirement.name: Prevent bug duplication; update existing or escalate/flag if no parent exists

requirement.requirement: Before creating any requirement, story, feature, or epic in brain/machine_artifacts/content/agile_backlog.json, Claude MUST search the backlog for a semantically duplicate or closely-related existing entry and update the existing record rather than create a new one when a match is found. Updates MUST focus on conciseness, accuracy, and fidelity to the evidence. When the entry is novel, Claude MUST insert it under a logical parent — requirement under story, story under feature, feature under epic. When no logical parent exists: in Normal or Idiot Mode (v4-004) Claude MUST escalate to human and wait for a decision before inserting; in Unattended Mode Claude MUST insert the entry with orphan = true under the nearest ancestor, flag it for human's async review, and proceed with its work.
requirement.name: Search backlog for duplicates before inserting new agile artifacts

requirement.requirement: ChatHealthy.AI brain content MUST be persisted on disk under brain/machine_artifacts/content/ and nowhere else. Claude Code's and Cursor's harness-managed Markdown files — CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/*.md, MEMORY.md and Claude's auto-memory topic files under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ — are NOT brain storage. Those MD files are reserved for harness instructions (CLAUDE.md family) or Claude's ungoverned working memory (MEMORY.md, per v4-037) and MUST NOT carry brain content. @-imports from CLAUDE.md that point at brain JSON files are the required mechanism to make brain content runtime-resident — they do not move the content into the MD file; the content stays on disk in JSON under brain/machine_artifacts/content/. Governing rule: v4-040.
requirement.name: Persist brain content only in brain/machine_artifacts/content/, not in MD files

requirement.requirement: When any of bugs.json, engineering_rules.json, or agile_backlog.json is edited during a session, Claude MUST flush the stale copy from its context and reload the current on-disk version before taking any further action governed by that file. The in-context copy MUST NOT lag the on-disk canonical copy across any action that reads or reasons about the file.
requirement.name: Flush and reload updated JSON files before any governed action

requirement.requirement: The system MUST write a byte-stream copy of brain/machine_artifacts/content/agile_backlog.json to test_output/req_index.txt at every UserPromptSubmit boot and at every session_end. Each write MUST overwrite any prior file at that path. test_output/ MUST be a gitignored project-local folder. CLAUDE.md MUST @-import test_output/req_index.txt. The canonical agile_backlog.json MUST remain the single authoritative source of backlog content. session_end MUST delete the prior test_output/req_index.txt before writing its regenerated copy. The copy format MUST be newline-delimited pipe-separated fields, one requirement per line, columns in order: epic_id, feature_id, story_id, req_id, priority, status, approval, orphan, requirement_text.
requirement.name: Write byte-stream copy of agile_backlog.json to test_output/req_index.txt on key

story.name: BrainContent JSONS reside in projectRoot/brain/machine_artifacts/Content
Foreign-key referential integrity across brain JSONs and code
story.description: FK references in brain JSONs and in repository code MUST resolve to a canonical id that exists in the source-of-truth backlog. Dangling FKs created by migrations, deletions, or renames MUST be tracked as bugs and remediated before the gate they break (e.g., commit or deploy).

requirement.name: Resolve all FK references to a canonical id or the ORPHAN sentinel
requirement.requirement: Every FK field in any brain JSON or repository code MUST hold either (a) a canonical id that exists in agile_backlog.json, or (b) the literal sentinel string 'ORPHAN' meaning the link is intentionally unresolved. Any other value is a bug and MUST be tracked under this requirement until remediated.

feature.name: DevOps — Build, Deploy, and Environment Management
feature.description: A software engineering discipline that unifies development and operations through automation, continuous delivery, and shared responsibility to accelerate the delivery of reliable software systems.

story.name: Universal deploy contract
story.description: The contract every deploy script obeys, regardless of environment. Port assignments, atomicity, version-document handling, build-bump rule, smoke-test invocation contract, and the human-authorization gate live here as the single source of truth.

requirement.name: Port table
requirement.requirement: Canonical port assignments, identical across all environments (local, dev, qa, prod): port 80 (HTTP — 301 redirects to HTTPS), port 443 (Website wrapper — public HTTPS entry), port 7860 (FindCare backend), port 8001 (EvaluateCare backend), port 8002 (SharedServices backend + React frontend). Every other requirement that names a port MUST refer to this requirement; MUST NOT restate the table.

requirement.name: Atomic deploy
requirement.requirement: Each deploy script either succeeds totally or fails totally with the environment torn down. There is no half-deployed third state. Atomicity is enforced by tearing down the previous environment as the first step (precondition; the ports in REQ-T-001 cannot host two services simultaneously).

requirement.name: Target readiness check
requirement.requirement: Before any deploy action, the script verifies the target environment is reachable and able to receive a deployment. For local: every port in REQ-T-001 is reachable on the host. For deployed envs: the target HuggingFace Space exists and accepts GitHub Actions pushes.

requirement.name: Build, start, verify
requirement.requirement: The script builds all components, starts them, then waits until every component responds as expected. The components are: FindCare backend, EvaluateCare backend, SharedServices backend (serving the React frontend), the public HTTPS entry (Website wrapper for local; Cloudflare Pages for deployed envs), and the front-end MongoDB cluster (tested as available, never deployed).

requirement.name: Smoke test invocation
requirement.requirement: After build/start/verify, the script invokes the master smoke test (S-006) with the target environment as parameter. On smoke-test failure the script MUST request explicit human verification before tearing down the environment, so the operator can inspect the failed state. Atomic teardown (REQ-B-001) proceeds only after the human authorizes it. Verification type = UAT (the human-verify gate on smoke failure cannot be auto-tested without stubbing the human, which defeats the requirement); UAT step lives in Code/deploy/local_deploy.py.

requirement.name: Step notices
requirement.requirement: Between every significant deploy step the script emits a notice via the mechanism defined in S-007. No bell rings unless explicitly instructed by the operator per S-007.

requirement.name: Human authorization gate
requirement.requirement: Every deploy — local, dev, qa, prod — pauses and requires explicit human authorization (interactive confirmation or signed approval token) before the production-affecting action begins. There are no unattended deploys now or in the foreseeable future. Production deploys carry the same gate as any other; what differs in prod is the version/framework ID assignment that follows (see S-004).

requirement.name: Version document
requirement.requirement: Build, version, and framework identifiers live as a single MongoDB document on the front-end cluster `chathealthyfrontend`, in the global database `admin`, in the collection literally named `Versions`. Each change inserts a new record carrying all three fields (build, version, framework) plus a `from` timestamp; the latest record by `from` is the current state. All three backend /health endpoints read the latest record. Build is incremented by the build-bump rule (REQ-T-003). Version and framework are set only by humans during prod deploy (S-004). Deploy pipelines never write these fields directly; the rule and the human routine are the only writers.

requirement.name: Build-bump rule
requirement.requirement: An engineering rule (Rule-063 in `engineering_rules.json`) executes as a post-commit hook on every commit not part of a deploy pipeline. Statement 1: insert a new `admin.Versions` record with build incremented by exactly one; version and framework copied forward unchanged. Statement 2: push the new values to the running Kafka producer's `/version_bump` endpoint so subsequent messages carry the new build stamp without the producer re-reading MongoDB.

requirement.name: Atomic teardown precondition
requirement.requirement: Before build, the script wipes prior artifacts and running processes (including Docker containers) and verifies every port in REQ-T-001 is clear. The wipe is the precondition that enables atomicity (REQ-B-001).

requirement.name: Structured deploy output
requirement.requirement: The script writes a structured output file Claude can read to {projectRoot}/test_output/deploy/ with the environment name and timestamp in the filename. Contents: pass/fail per test, container IDs (or PIDs for the Website wrapper), port assignments (per REQ-T-001), timestamps, and errors.

requirement.name: Pytest exit propagation
requirement.requirement: When piping pytest output through tee, the script uses PIPESTATUS[0] (not $?) to capture the pytest exit code. On any pytest step failure, SMOKE TEST FAILED MUST be displayed to the human operator on the controlling terminal (not silently logged) so the operator can act before any teardown decision per REQ-B-004.

requirement.name: React frontend build
requirement.requirement: Each deploy script builds the React frontend with the backend API URL for the target environment baked in, pointing to the service serving the React frontend per S-001-REQ-T-001 (post-S-008 migration: SharedServices on port 8002). Local and deployed envs differ only in the domain portion of the URL.

story.name: Local-only deploy
story.description: What is unique to deploying on the developer's workstation. Backend services run as local Docker containers per the port table (S-001-REQ-T-001). MongoDB connections target the dev front-end cluster — the only resource shared with dev. The Website wrapper, which binds privileged ports 80 and 443, runs as a host-OS process (Docker exception). All other deploy facts live in S-001 and S-003.

requirement.name: Backend containers
requirement.requirement: All three backend services (FindCare, EvaluateCare, SharedServices) run as local Docker containers built from each backend's Dockerfile and requirements.txt. The local runtime MUST NOT import any Python package not installed by the container's pip install. Ports per S-001-REQ-T-001.

requirement.name: Website wrapper on host OS
requirement.requirement: The Website wrapper, binding the privileged ports in S-001-REQ-T-001, MUST run as a host-OS process rather than a Docker container.

requirement.name: Shared dev MongoDB
requirement.requirement: When deploying locally, all backend services connect to the dev front-end MongoDB cluster (cluster `chathealthyfrontend`, database `dev_*`). This is the only resource shared between local and dev. All other state, services, and ports are local.

story.name: Deployed-env deploy (dev/qa/prod)
story.description: What is unique to deploying to the dev, qa, or prod environments. A single script accepts the environment as parameter and pushes to the matching HuggingFace paid Space (Docker, lowest tier) via GitHub Actions. Cloudflare Pages serves the static chathealthy.ai site for these envs.

requirement.name: Single parameterized script
requirement.requirement: One deploy script accepts an environment parameter (dev | qa | prod) and pushes to the corresponding HuggingFace paid Space. Logic is identical across the three environments except for prod-only behaviors (S-004) and the absence of non-prod display chrome (S-005) in prod.

requirement.name: HuggingFace README preservation
requirement.requirement: Every HuggingFace Space deploy preserves the target Space's README.md across the push. README.md carries the HF Space frontmatter configuration (sdk, python_version, license) and MUST NOT be wiped. Missing README.md after a deploy is a violation.

requirement.name: Cloudflare HTTP→HTTPS
requirement.requirement: Every Cloudflare Pages deployment of chathealthy.ai (dev, qa, prod) 301-redirects every http:// request to its https:// equivalent. The redirect is immediate (no intermediate response, no caching delay) and applies to every path. The deploy script MUST verify this setting and configure it if absent.

requirement.name: Cloudflare 404 error page
requirement.requirement: Cloudflare Pages returns HTTP 404 for unknown paths and renders a dedicated error page (not a blank response, not a redirect, not the home page). CloudFlare's default convention of redirecting unknown paths to the site root MUST be explicitly disabled. The deploy script verifies this setting and configures it if absent.

story.name: Prod-only behaviors
story.description: The only differences between prod and the dev/qa environments, aside from their different addresses, are: (1) the chrome banner with versions and navigation between the servers does not appear in prod, and (2) the security GUI widget does not appear in prod.

requirement.name: Version & framework ID assignment
requirement.requirement: When environment=prod, after human UAT sign-off, the deploy script accepts human-supplied values for a new version ID (and potentially a new framework ID) and writes them to the version document (per S-001-REQ-T-002). Dev and qa deploys never change these fields. No automation, ever, sets version or framework.

requirement.name: Display chrome OFF
requirement.requirement: In prod, the non-prod display chrome (S-005) MUST NOT render: no environment banner, no security token panel, no service-switching buttons. The smoke test (S-006) skips display-chrome checks when env=prod via its macro-variance dimension.

story.name: Non-prod display chrome
story.description: Display chrome visible in local, dev, and qa; absent in prod (see S-004-REQ-B-002). Owns the environment banner, the security-token panel, and the three service-switching buttons. Banner reads /health from whichever service currently owns the page (FindCare, EvaluateCare, or SharedServices).

requirement.name: Banner contents
requirement.requirement: The environment banner displays environment label (LOCAL/DEV/QA), version, framework, and build, fetched from the /health endpoint of whichever service currently owns the page. All values render on one line with sufficient spacing for human readability. The banner displays the active service name in brackets (e.g., [evaluatecare]).

requirement.name: Banner re-fetches on ownership transfer
requirement.requirement: When page ownership transfers between services, the banner re-fetches /health from the new owner and updates inline.

requirement.name: Service buttons + active is cold
requirement.requirement: Three service-switching buttons (FindCare, EvaluateCare, SharedServices) appear in the banner. The currently-active service's button is cold (greyed, disabled); on click it shows tooltip 'You are here already'. The other two buttons are hot (clickable, styled). Clicking a hot button transfers page ownership to that service, which then controls the entire frame. The content of this display must be served by the HuggingFace server that owns the content.

requirement.name: Unimplemented placeholder
requirement.requirement: The center panel displays the service name and 'is still unimplemented.' when SharedServices or EvaluateCare has control, until those services have real implementations. The content of this display must be served by the HuggingFace server that owns the content.

requirement.name: Security token panel
requirement.requirement: Each service displays a security token panel rendered per the mock at {projectRoot}/brain/machine_artifacts/diagramsAndImages/GUIImagesAndMockUps/NonProdSecuriytToken.jpg. Right panel and lower regions display the security information defined by EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-B-007. The content of this display must be served by the HuggingFace server that owns the content.

story.name: Smoke test
story.description: One master Playwright pytest (`Code/deploy/localSmokeTestPyTest.py`) runs against any environment. The script varies along three dimensions: (1) environment — localhost / dev / qa / prod; (2) macro variance — display chrome (banner, token, service buttons) is exercised in non-prod and skipped in prod per S-004-REQ-B-002; (3) micro variance — PKI certificates differ across environments and the cert-verification step asserts the env-appropriate cert is in use. The actual script is the source of truth: where these requirements differ from the script's behavior, the script wins and these requirements MUST be reverse-engineered to match. Per-step requirements below (REQ-B-002 through REQ-B-037) capture each test class in the script.

requirement.name: Master smoke-test contract
requirement.requirement: `localSmokeTestPyTest.py` is the single master smoke test. It accepts the target environment as a parameter and exercises every step below in declared order. Every step MUST pass for the smoke test to PASS overall.

requirement.name: Step 00 — Build gate: local and dev report identical build
requirement.requirement: Smoke test fetches /health from local FindCare and dev FindCare and asserts the `build` field matches across the two envs. Two environments on the same build MUST be running identical code and configuration; mismatched builds halt the smoke test before any further steps.

requirement.name: Step 01 — HTTP→HTTPS redirect
requirement.requirement: Browser navigation to http://{domain} MUST 301-redirect to https://{domain}. The smoke test deliberately probes the insecure scheme (constructed at runtime) and asserts the final URL is https://.

requirement.name: Step 02 — Banner shows env label, version, framework, build
requirement.requirement: The environment banner element (`#envBanner`) MUST be visible and contain the env label (LOCAL/DEV/QA), and the literal strings `Version: <v>`, `Framework: <f>`, `Build: <b>` whose values match the response from the active service's /health.

requirement.name: Step 03 — SharedServices button is a banner button
requirement.requirement: A `<button>` with `data-service='sharedservices'` MUST exist inside `#envBanner` (not in any header nav), MUST be visible, and its label MUST be `SharedServices` (PascalCase, no space).

requirement.name: Step 04 — Splash renders welcome words
requirement.requirement: The chat iframe loads. The first 10 words of the canonical welcome message (per `_get_welcome_words()`) MUST appear in the iframe body text.

requirement.name: Step 05 — Chat input enabled and focused on click
requirement.requirement: The chat input element (`input[placeholder*='Type a message']` or textarea) MUST be visible, MUST NOT carry a `disabled` attribute, and MUST become focused when clicked.

requirement.name: Step 06 — Search returns providers
requirement.requirement: Submitting `Find me a bone doctor in Delaware` MUST yield results containing NPI strings (`NPI[:\s]+\d{10}`) in the iframe body within the chat timeout. The smoke test captures the originating session token for downstream nonce comparisons.

requirement.name: Step 07 — Specialty checkboxes appear in left panel
requirement.requirement: After a search, `#leftPanel` MUST contain at least one `input[type='checkbox']` representing a specialty.

requirement.name: Step 08 — Left panel cell layout and scroll cap
requirement.requirement: The left panel MUST contain exactly four `[data-cell]` cells (1..4) with reactive percentage heights 18/40/20/22 (declared via `flex:0 0 N%` or `height:N%` — pixel heights are forbidden). An Uncheck All / Check All toggle MUST live inside cell 1 (the green header). With more than 12 prescribers present, no more than 12 specialty checkboxes may be visible in cell 2 without scrolling.

requirement.name: Step 09 — Provider NPIs in center frame
requirement.requirement: The chat iframe body MUST contain provider NPI strings (`NPI[:\s]+\d{10}`) after the search resolves.

requirement.name: Step 10 — Bottom panel zero before selection
requirement.requirement: The chat iframe body MUST contain `0 / 5` (or `0/5`) reflecting an empty Selected for Evaluation panel before any provider is selected.

requirement.name: Step 11 — Select up to three providers
requirement.requirement: Up to three provider Select-for-Evaluation buttons MUST be clickable; the smoke test clicks min(count, 3) of them.

requirement.name: Step 12 — Selected providers appear in bottom panel
requirement.requirement: After selection, the iframe body MUST include the words `SELECTED` and `EVALUATION` and the count must read 1..5 / 5 (no longer 0).

requirement.name: Step 13 — Evaluate button click
requirement.requirement: An Evaluate button (`#guiEvalBtn` or text-matched `Evaluate`) MUST be present and clickable; the smoke test clicks it to trigger handoff to EvaluateCare.

requirement.name: Step 14 — EvaluateCare has frame control
requirement.requirement: After the Evaluate click, the chat iframe (`#coreChatFrame`) MUST be hidden and `#evalcareSplash` MUST be visible — EvaluateCare owns the frame.

requirement.name: Step 15 — mTLS to EvaluateCare TLS 1.2+
requirement.requirement: An mTLS handshake from the smoke test (using FindCare's client cert + key against the CA cert) to localhost:EVALCARE_PORT MUST succeed with TLS version 1.2 or higher. Failure of the handshake (SSLError) is a hard failure.

requirement.name: Step 16 — Right panel shows EvaluateCare + provider NPIs
requirement.requirement: `#rightPanel` text MUST contain `EVALUATECARE` (case-insensitive substring) and at least one 10-digit NPI string after the EvaluateCare handoff.

requirement.name: Step 17 — Token same sent/received; positioned below specialties
requirement.requirement: The handoff FindCare→EvaluateCare MUST yield a fresh nonce; the session GUID MUST remain identical. The session token element (`#guiSessionCell` or `#guiSessionId`) MUST be positioned below the specialty list (its bounding-box `y` must be greater than the bottom of the scroll container), not beside it.

requirement.name: Step 18 — Token components in distinct colors in both panels
requirement.requirement: Both right panel and left panel MUST show signed-token components in distinct colors: signed token in indigo (`#6366f1`), nonce in amber (`#d97706`), GUID in teal (`#0b7a75`). Right and left panels MUST present the same color treatment.

requirement.name: Step 19 — Nonce changed after EvaluateCare handoff; GUID preserved
requirement.requirement: After the FindCare→EvaluateCare handoff, the EvaluateCare-side nonce MUST differ from the original FindCare nonce; the EvaluateCare-side GUID MUST equal the original GUID.

requirement.name: Step 20 — EvaluateCare splash text
requirement.requirement: `#evalcareSplash` MUST be visible and contain the literal strings `EvaluateCare` and `is still unimplemented`.

requirement.name: Step 21 — Filter toggle change
requirement.requirement: Clicking the first specialty `[data-gui-action='filter-toggle']` checkbox MUST register and trigger the gui:reset path on apply. The toggle clicked MUST be a specialty filter-toggle (not a filter-provider-type) so that the return to FindCare proceeds via gui:reset.

requirement.name: Step 22 — Apply filter returns control to FindCare
requirement.requirement: Clicking `[data-gui-action='filter-apply']` MUST: (1) restore visibility of `#coreChatFrame`; (2) hide both `#evalcareSplash` and `#sharedSplash`; (3) cause the FindCare welcome message to repaint (≥20 of the first 25 welcome words present in the iframe body within ~15 seconds).

requirement.name: Step 23 — Chat input visible and focused after return
requirement.requirement: After return to FindCare, the chat input element MUST be visible and focused within the polling window (15 retries / 1s).

requirement.name: Step 24 — Nonce changed on EvaluateCare→FindCare return
requirement.requirement: The handoff EvaluateCare→FindCare MUST yield a fresh nonce different from both the original FindCare nonce and the EvaluateCare nonce; the GUID MUST remain unchanged.

requirement.name: Step 25 — SharedServices button push: direct, not proxied
requirement.requirement: Clicking the SharedServices banner button MUST result in: (1) `#rightPanel` showing `Shared Services`; (2) at least one POST to `<SHARED_URL>/verify-token` directly (not proxied through FindCare's `/shared/verify-token`); (3) `#rightPanel` text containing `Server, serving security token: SharedServices` (self-identifying responding service, not the token signer).

requirement.name: Step 26 — SharedServices has frame control
requirement.requirement: After the SharedServices push, `#coreChatFrame` MUST be hidden and `#sharedSplash` MUST be visible.

requirement.name: Step 27 — mTLS to SharedServices TLS 1.2+
requirement.requirement: An mTLS handshake from the smoke test (using FindCare's client cert + key against the CA cert) to localhost:SHARED_PORT MUST succeed with TLS version 1.2 or higher.

requirement.name: Step 28 — SharedServices splash text
requirement.requirement: `#sharedSplash` MUST be visible and contain the literal strings `Shared Services` and `is still unimplemented`.

requirement.name: Step 29 — SharedServices token auth: GUID preserved, nonce fresh
requirement.requirement: `#rightPanel` header MUST read `SHARED SERVICES` (case-insensitive). The handoff FindCare→SharedServices MUST yield a fresh nonce; GUID MUST equal the original.

requirement.name: Step 30 — SharedServices nonce/GUID stored and verified
requirement.requirement: The SharedServices-side nonce and GUID captured in step 29 MUST be present in test state; the GUID MUST equal the original FindCare GUID.

requirement.name: Step 31 — Handoff 4: SharedServices→FindCare via filter
requirement.requirement: Clicking a specialty checkbox and Apply Filter MUST return control to FindCare (`#coreChatFrame` visible). The handoff MUST yield a fresh nonce.

requirement.name: Step 32 — Handoff 5: EvaluateCare→SharedServices direct
requirement.requirement: After re-selecting a provider and clicking Evaluate, then clicking the SharedServices banner button from the EvaluateCare context, `#rightPanel` MUST show `Shared Services`. The handoff MUST yield a fresh nonce.

requirement.name: Step 33 — Handoff 6: SharedServices→EvaluateCare via re-evaluate
requirement.requirement: Returning to FindCare via filter, then re-selecting and clicking Evaluate, MUST hand control to EvaluateCare directly from the SharedServices→FindCare path. The handoff MUST yield a fresh nonce.

requirement.name: Step 34 — All four services respond on HTTPS with expected JSON
requirement.requirement: Final assertion: `GET https://<BASE_URL>/` returns HTTP 200; `GET <FINDCARE_URL>/health` returns JSON with `status=="ok"`; `GET <EVALCARE_URL>/health` returns JSON with `service=="evaluate_care"`; `GET <SHARED_URL>/health` returns JSON with `service=="shared_services"`.

requirement.name: Step 35 — Comprehensive PKI certificate verification (NEW)
requirement.requirement: The smoke test MUST hold the public certs of every server participating in mTLS (FindCare, EvaluateCare, SharedServices) and assert: (a) every cert file in {projectRoot}/Code/Shared/ops/certs/ parses as a valid PKI X.509 certificate, is signed by the project's CA cert (ca.crt), and is not expired; (b) for each ordered server pair (FindCare↔EvaluateCare, FindCare↔SharedServices, EvaluateCare↔SharedServices), an mTLS handshake succeeds in BOTH directions using the appropriate client cert against the CA. The point of the step is to assert real mutual-PKI rather than any subset (Steps 15 and 27 cover only FindCare→EvaluateCare and FindCare→SharedServices; this step fills the gap and adds explicit cert-validity checks).

story.name: Step notices and human-instructed bell
story.description: On-screen notices at significant deploy steps (the mechanism for S-001-REQ-B-005). The bell is HUMAN-INSTRUCTED ONLY: it never rings as default behavior. Default deploy behavior is silent except for the on-screen notices.

requirement.name: Step notices
requirement.requirement: At each significant deploy step the script MUST display an on-screen notice. Significant steps are: (1) deploy started for {environment}; (2) old environment torn down and ready to receive new; (3) new environment built; (4) smoke test started; (5) smoke test ended, with ratio (passed/total) of assertions and list of any failures.

requirement.name: Bell rings only on explicit human instruction
requirement.requirement: The bell MUST NOT ring by default. The human operator may instruct Claude (via IDE prompt, command-line flag, or other explicit invocation) to ring the bell at specific times, in specific patterns. The operator chooses both WHEN and HOW. There is no requirement for unattended-deploy bell behavior; all deploys are human-supervised (per S-001-REQ-B-006).

story.name: React serving migration (opportunistic architectural evolution, one-time)
story.description: ONE-TIME architectural evolution included opportunistically in this deploy-management feature. Moves the React frontend serving responsibility from FindCare (port 7860) to SharedServices (port 8002). After this story ships, it is permanently done — it does NOT belong to the enduring deploy facts and never re-fires.

requirement.name: React serving moves to SharedServices
requirement.requirement: After this story ships, SharedServices (port 8002 per S-001-REQ-T-001) serves the React frontend in addition to its backend. FindCare (port 7860) serves only the FindCare backend. No other behavioral change.

requirement.name: Build URLs updated
requirement.requirement: S-001-REQ-T-008 (the universal React build req) builds the React frontend with the SharedServices URL baked in. Pre-migration FindCare URL is removed from all build paths.

requirement.name: Smoke test passes post-migration
requirement.requirement: The master smoke test (S-006) passes against an environment where SharedServices serves the React frontend, with no regression in any of the current step set (Step00..Step34 plus the cert-verification step in S-006-REQ-T-003 — currently 36 steps total).

feature.name: Audit — Technical, Business, Regulatory and Corporate Governance
feature.description: This feature encompasses all the audits that must be done to maintain technical and business history, integrity and regulatory and corporate governance.

story.description: A deterministic Python orchestrator dispatches disposable AI workers to analyze git history, brain artifacts, and current code to identify lost capabilities, undocumented changes, and gaps between intent and implementation. The orchestrator is 100% deterministic — all state is on disk, all decisions are file-existence checks. AI is used only inside workers for code analysis. Audits MUST NOT create state changes — they only maintain their own notes and documents, and produce findings and recommendations. The orchestrator loops until all jobs are complete or a human sets the stop command in the control file.

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST examine every version of every file in the git repository to establish a complete lineage of what was built, changed, and removed.
requirement.name: Audit all file versions for complete git repository lineage

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST identify every capability that the brain documents as intended but that does not exist in the current codebase. The brain is the authoritative source of intent.
requirement.name: Identify capabilities intended by brain but missing from current codebase

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST identify every capability that was built and subsequently lost due to uncontrolled changes, code rollbacks, or data loss.
requirement.name: Audit identifies capabilities lost via uncontrolled change, rollback, or data

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST identify every AI call, system prompt, and LLM integration that existed in any previous version and determine whether it is active, intentionally replaced, or lost.
requirement.name: Audit all past AI calls, prompts, LLMs; flag active, replaced, or lost ones

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST cross-reference all findings against the agile backlog, bugs, design documents, business plan, work log, punch lists, unrealized ideas, and all other brain artifacts to determine whether each loss is documented or undocumented.
requirement.name: Audit cross-checks findings against all artifacts for documented or undocumented

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST produce findings categorized as: undocumented losses, documented but unplanned recoveries, and intentional replacements. Each finding MUST include evidence from git history or brain artifacts.
requirement.name: Categorize audit findings; each must include git or brain evidence

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST produce actionable recommendations for each finding, prioritized by user impact, with effort estimates and a proposed recovery approach.
requirement.name: Audit recommendations prioritized by user impact with effort and recovery plan

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST be repeatable. Running the audit again on the same codebase MUST produce the same findings. The audit is idempotent.
requirement.name: Audit must be repeatable and idempotent, yielding same findings on same codebase

requirement.requirement: The audit output MUST be consumable by both humans (readable report) and machines (structured JSON). The CEO is the primary consumer.
requirement.name: Audit output as human-readable report and structured JSON for CEO consumption

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST NOT modify any source code, database records, brain files, or deployed artifacts. It is a read-only operation. Output is limited to the audit directory only.
requirement.name: Audit is read-only, modifies nothing, output limited to audit directory

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST run to completion autonomously without requiring human intervention beyond the initial start command.
requirement.name: Audit runs autonomously to completion after initial start command

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST survive infrastructure failures (crashes, restarts, context loss) and resume from the last completed unit of work.
requirement.name: Audit recovers from failures and resumes from last completed unit of work

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST track and report its own cost (token consumption) as part of its output.
requirement.name: Audit must track and report its own token consumption in its output

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST have numbered findings where the most important findings are at the top with the lowest number and the least important findings have the highest numbers.
requirement.name: Audit findings numbered by importance, highest priority at top

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST make recommendations based on the findings of how to address and remediate each finding.
requirement.name: Audit must recommend remediations for each finding

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST describe its methodology at the top of the report.
requirement.name: Audit report must include methodology description at the top

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST document its assumptions under methodology and above findings.
requirement.name: Audit documents assumptions under methodology and above findings

requirement.requirement: Each audit finding MUST be supported with evidence of at least one example from both the codebase (which may be that no code exists) and from the brain (a known best practice, a brain artifact reference, or code with file and line ranges).
requirement.name: Audit finding must cite code and brain evidence examples

requirement.requirement: The orchestrator MUST be a pure Python script with no AI dependencies. All decisions MUST be based on file existence checks and JSON parsing. No LLM calls in the orchestrator.
requirement.name: Pure Python orchestrator with file checks, JSON parsing, no AI or LLM calls

requirement.requirement: The orchestrator MUST loop continuously until all jobs are complete or a human sets the command to stop in the control file. No other mechanism may stop the orchestrator.
requirement.name: Orchestrator loops until all jobs finish or control file stop command is set

requirement.requirement: All orchestrator state MUST be persisted to disk in a control file (control.json). The orchestrator MUST NOT depend on Claude Code context or conversation memory for any decision.
requirement.name: Persist orchestrator state to control.json; no reliance on memory for decisions

story.description: Two-pass scanner: Pass 1 streams every source file, builds a map of all definitions (classes, methods, functions) and all references (calls, imports, attribute access). Pass 2 reconciles — anything defined but never referenced is dead and must be deleted. Two modes: check-in (staged files only, fast) and full regression (entire codebase).

requirement.requirement: Pass 1 must stream source files without holding full source in memory. It accumulates a definitions map (name, file, line) and a references set (names used). Memory proportional to symbol count, not source size. DR-008 compliant.
requirement.name: Stream pass 1 source, accumulate symbol maps, memory ~symbol count, DR-008

requirement.requirement: Pass 2 walks the definitions map and checks each against the references set. Any definition with zero references and no framework-invocation decorator (FastAPI route, Azure trigger, governance hook) is reported as dead code.
requirement.name: Report unreferenced definitions without framework decorators as dead code in Pas

requirement.requirement: Check-in mode scans only staged files (git diff --cached). If a staged file adds a function, verify something calls it. If it deletes a function, verify nothing else calls it. Must complete in under 5 seconds for typical commits.
requirement.name: Check-in scans staged files for function usage and finishes under 5 seconds

requirement.requirement: Dead code found during check-in mode blocks the commit. Dead code found during full regression is reported but does not block (informational for promotion review).
requirement.name: Block commits for dead code in check-in; report only in full regression

story.name: Run Time Error Management
story.description: Defines and enforces runtime error behavior for the ChatHealthy.AI front-end application. This story covers how the application surfaces failures to users, how it interacts with backend services under failure conditions.

requirement.name: Fatal error full-screen display in index.html
requirement.requirement: For every error that is fatal — meaning any error condition whatsoever that is not explicitly required in a written requirement to be less than fatal — index.html is to display the following: In a large font and centered: 'HTTP 503: Fatal Error, this service is not available.' In a smaller font and centered: Line 1: link to HTTPS://{current environment}.chathealthy.ai. Line 2: If you get this error repeatedly and wish to call our team, please call Skip Snow @ 646 408 8999. Line 3: If you prefer email skip's email is: skip@chatHealthy.ai. Line 4: smaller text that wraps, the error message returned from an API. If the error is from the JavaScript without a call to an API then the error message will be 'JS routine {failed}'. Line 5: we apologize for this problem.

requirement.name: Internal API error responses must not reveal application facts
requirement.requirement: Every API that index.html calls that is internal to ChatHealthy.ai's servers must, when they encounter errors, return an error message that is not sufficiently clear that it would reveal any significant fact about the application. The error message can cite the API that failed, the rough-grained source of the error, and the time of the error.

requirement.name: API errors must log a detailed message for later debugging
requirement.requirement: Any API that does encounter an error must log a detailed message about the error so that it can be debugged later.

requirement.name: All ChatHealthy.ai web servers redirect HTTP to HTTPS
